abstract.para: While the system to be protected is up and running, create a file backup and generate a recovery system that contains a system-specific &rear; recovery installer.
After you have configured &rear; as described in , create the recovery installation system (including the &rear; recovery installer) plus the file backup.

listitem.para: For basic backups with tar, use the rear mkbackup command to create both the file backup and the recovery system.
For third-party backup tools, use the rear mkrescue command to create the recovery system, and use the third-party backup tool to create the file backup.
&rear; is installed on the system you want to back up.

example.title: Creating a recovery system with a basic tar backup

step.para: Log in either as the &rootuser; user or as a user with sudo privileges.
Run the rear mkbackup command with the -D option to enable verbose mode and debug mode:
This command performs the following steps:

listitem.para: Analyzes the target system and gathers information, in particular about the disk layout (partitioning, file systems, mount points) and about the boot loader.

Creates a bootable recovery system with the information gathered in the first step. The resulting &rear; recovery installer is specific to the system that you want to protect from disaster. It can only be used to re-create this specific system.
Calls the internal backup tool to back up system files and user files.

step.para: Depending on your &rear; configuration, you might need to create a recovery medium by copying the recovery system to a USB . Alternatively, you can use a network boot via PXE.

example.title: Creating a recovery system with a third-party backup

step.para: Log in either as the &rootuser; user or as a user with sudo privileges.
Run the rear mkrescue command with the -D option to enable verbose mode and debug mode:
This command performs the following steps:

listitem.para: Analyzes the target system and gathers information, in particular about the disk layout (partitioning, file systems, mount points) and about the boot loader.

Creates a bootable recovery system with the information gathered in the first step. The resulting &rear; recovery installer is specific to the system that you want to protect from disaster. It can only be used to re-create this specific system.

important.para: This command doesn't create a backup of the files.

step.para: Create a file backup using your third-party backup tool.
Depending on your &rear; configuration, you might need to create a recovery medium by copying the recovery system to a USB . Alternatively, you can use a network boot via PXE.
